cues.text: Good afternoon everyone. In today’s seminar we are going to continue listening to different students giving us a presentation on the subject of their term paper.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Now today is Hillary’s turn. So, what are you going to talk about today   Hillary?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Well, some of you will know that I was brought up when I was young in Japan and I’m going to do my term paper on Japan’s bullet trains, which have revolutionized their rail industry.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: Japan’s main island Honshu is covered by a network of high speed train lines that connect Tokyo with most of the island’s major cities and Fukuoka on the island of Kyushu.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: Japan’s high-speed trains are called shinkansen but are known to us bullet trains.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: The Japanese bullettrain system is credited with being the world’s first purpose-built high-speed railway, and the model and inspiration for all other similar type systems running today such as the French TGV.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: The reputation it has earned for safety, speed and punctuality is unsurpassed . I’d like to give you some figures about that.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: As regards safety, there has never been a death on the bullet train system since it’s inception in 1964, other than that caused by deliberate passenger misadventure.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: As far as speed is concerned the bullet train holds the current world records for the fastest average speed between two station stops, which was 260 1.8 kph between Hiroshima and Kokura.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: The train travelled 192 kilometers in 44 minutes. This record is from the 500 series “Nozomi” trains running at a maximum speed of 300 kilometers an hour between Shin-Osaka and Hakata.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: I’ll talk more about them later. The punctuality puts European train services to shame. Most trains arrive at their destination, after several hours, to within the second!
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: In one year, the total time that all bullets trains were late by was 12 seconds! This statistic is hard to believe but it would be difficult to prove otherwise and that’s what the rail authorities in Japan have told us.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: Now I’d like to tell you a bit about their history. The first bullet train was introduced in 1964 by Central & West Japan Railways for the Tokyo to Osaka route.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: Most of these old trains have now been discontinued . There have been several bullet train models since then.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: The most recent ones have been the 300, 500 and 700 series and it’s the 500 series one that can travel at 300 kph. The bullet trains operating in Japan today are of the three following categories: Nozomi, Hikari and Kodama.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: The Nozomi trains stop only at the most important stations, and reach Osaka from Tokyo in only about two and a half hours and it’s the most modern of bullet trains that serve as Nozomi.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: Hikari trains stop a little bit more frequently than Nozomi trains, and need roughly three hours to reach Osaka from Tokyo.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: Kodama trains stop at all stations and they are the local trains among bullet trains. Older models of bullet trains serve as Kodama.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: I’d like now to talk a little bit about the technology involved in bullet trains. The Shinkansen bullet trains consist of electrically powered cars.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: That means basically all individual cars are equippedwith electric motor driving systems. This is in contrast to locomotive trains in which the locomotive pulls the passenger coaches .
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: The realization of the high-speed Shinkansen with the electric train system had a great significance
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: The French “Train a Grande Vitesse” or TGV runs on a centralised power system, in which the heavyweight, high-output locomotives at both ends pull the passenger coaches. It’s a system suitable to European railways , which run basically on straight tracks in wide plains with solid foundations.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: However it is unsuitable in Japan where the ground is flimsy and the tracks full of curves and undulations and inter-city distances are short, making it necessary for the trains to accelerate and decelerate frequently.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: One of the advantages of the electric car system is that the motor functions as a brake to reduce the speed of the train.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: When the power feed to the electric car motors is stopped, the wheels continue revolving , keeping the motors rotating, resulting in electricity generation by magnetic induction.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: As the force acts in the direction opposite to the axles motion , it functions as a brake to the train.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: All the motors equipped on each coach can be utilized effectively to reduce the speed, making the electric train system advantageous on Japanese railways, which involve frequent deceleration and acceleration.
cues.speaker: Hillary

cues.text: In addition, by virtue of the remarkable progress achieved recently in semiconductor technologies, the electric train system has undergone tremendous improvements in power, operability and safety administration, so the system is becoming increasingly advantageous.
cues.speaker: Hillary
